transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s mostly about my eating. I work all day and then I’ve been taking this evening class, and after that I sometimes stop for food, just meaning to get something quick. But then it turns into a full fast-food meal, and maybe candy from the vending machine—those machines are right there, you know, and I always think I’ll just get one thing—and then when I get home I’ll keep going with snacks, like I’m trying to make up for the whole day or something. It’s been bothering me.
When you find yourself eating this way, does it feel like you can’t control what or how much you’re eating?

Yeah… yeah, it does. Like once I start on those snacks, I’ll be telling myself, “Just close the bag, go to bed,” and then my hand is already back in there again. It’s stupid because I can balance accounts all day, you know, numbers have to come out right, everything in its column—but with that, I just… don’t seem to stop. I keep going until I feel embarrassed, kind of sick of myself.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do extra exercise to try to control your weight or how you feel about what you ate?

Um… yeah. Not all the time, but a few times after those late-night eating things, I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. I hate even saying that. It’s like I start thinking about how much I ate and how it’s going to show on me, and I panic a little.

I don’t really mess with laxatives, and exercise… I mean, I should exercise more in general, my doctor’s told me that before, but that’s not really what happens after. It’s more that vomiting thing, a few times.
